translations.text: The word of God that came to Jeremiah, son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who lived in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Hear the word of the Lord, house of Jacob and every clan of the house of Israel.
Therefore I will still bring a case against you, says the Lord, and I will bring a case against your children's children.
At that time they will call Jerusalem the throne of the Lord, and all nations will gather in Jerusalem in the name of the Lord. They will no longer follow the schemes of their evil hearts.
For this is what the Lord says to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem: Plow your fallow ground, and do not sow among thorns.
At that time you will say to this people and to Jerusalem: A wind of deception in the wilderness, on the path of the daughter of my people, neither for cleansing nor for purification.
Like guards of a field, they surrounded her, because you neglected me, says the Lord.
And I said: Perhaps they are poor; therefore they could not understand the ways of the Lord and the judgments of God.
For which of these things shall I be reconciled with you? Your children abandoned me and swore by those that are not gods. I fed them to the full, but they committed adultery and lodged in brothels.
Shall I not call them to account for all this, says the Lord? Shall my soul not seek vengeance on such a nation?
Our prophets became wind, and the word of the Lord was not in them. So may it happen to them.
Therefore this is what the Lord God Almighty says: Because you spoke these words, look, I have made my word in your mouth fire, and this people wood, and it will consume them.

For look, I will bring a nation from far away against you, house of Israel, says the Lord: an ancient nation, a nation from ages past, a nation whose language you will not understand and whose words you will not comprehend.
Shall I not call them to account for all this, says the Lord? Shall my soul not seek vengeance on such a nation?
For this is what the Lord of hosts says: Break down her wooden structures; cast an army against Jerusalem, for she is a city wholly false, with oppression within her.
And I appointed watchmen over you: Listen to the sound of the trumpet. But they say: We will not listen.
The word that came to Jeremiah from the Lord, saying:
Stand at the gate of the Lord's house and read these words there, and say: Hear the word of the Lord, all Judah, you who enter through these gates to worship the Lord.
And I will cast you out of my presence, as I cast out your brothers, all the offspring of Ephraim.

At that time, says the Lord, they will bring out of their graves the bones of the kings of Judah, the bones of their rulers, the bones of the priests, the bones of the prophets, and the bones of the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

Now why should we remain seated? Gather together, and let us enter the fortified cities and fall there, for the Lord our God has cast us down and given us bitter water to drink, because we sinned before him.
Oh, that my head were water and my eyes fountains of tears, so that I might weep day and night for this people and for the wounded of the daughter of my people!
And deceit upon deceit, and they refused to know me, says the Lord.
This is what the Lord says: Let the wise man not boast in his wisdom, let the mighty man not boast in his strength, and let the great man not boast in his greatness.

Rather, let those who boast boast in this: that they understand and know me, that I am the Lord who carries out justice, mercy, and righteousness on the earth. For these are the things I desire, says the Lord.
It is the Lord who made the earth by his power, established the world by his wisdom, and stretched out the heavens by his understanding.
Everyone has become foolish in his knowledge; every goldsmith has been put to shame by his carved images, for they have cast falsehood, and there is no breath in them.
I know, Lord, that a person's path is not his own, and no man can walk and make his own paths succeed.
Hear the words of this covenant, and speak to the men of Judah and the inhabitants of Jerusalem.

I commanded this to your fathers on the day when I brought them out of the land of Egypt, out of the iron furnace, saying: Hear my voice and do everything that I command you, and you shall be my people, and I shall be your God.
For I say concerning the beloved that he has committed abominations inside my temple. Will prayers and consecrated meat take away your evils from you, or will you be saved by such things?

And the Lord God of hosts, who planted you, has pronounced disaster against you in return for the evils of the house of Israel and the house of Judah, which they committed against themselves, provoking me to anger by offering incense to Baal.
But you, Lord, know me; you have seen me and tested my heart before you. Gather them like sheep for slaughter, and set them apart for the day of slaughter.
For even your brothers and your father's household have betrayed you; they have cried out after you and gathered against you. Do not trust them, for they will speak evil of you.
It has been laid waste to destruction. Because of me, the whole land has been utterly laid waste, for there is no one who takes it to heart.
And after I have uprooted them, I will return and have mercy on them, and settle them, each in his own inheritance and each in his own land.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:

And you shall speak this message to this people: Thus says the Lord God of Israel: Every wineskin shall be filled with wine. And if they say to you, Do we not know very well that every wineskin shall be filled with wine?
For your name's sake, stop; do not destroy the throne of your glory. Remember; do not break your covenant with us.
And the Lord said to me: Even if Moses and Samuel stood before me, my soul would not be with them. Send this people away from my presence, and let them go out.
And I will scatter them abroad at the gates of my people. They became childless, for I destroyed my people because of their evils, and they did not turn back.
Why do those who distress me grow strong, and why are my wounds severe? How shall I be healed? You have indeed become to me like cold water that cannot be trusted.
And I will cast you out of this land into a land that neither you nor your fathers have known. There you shall serve foreign gods day and night, and they will show you no mercy.
Therefore, behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when they will no longer say: As the Lord lives, who brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt.
And on the mountains of the countryside I will give your strength and all your treasures as plunder, and your high places, because of sins throughout all your borders.
Thus the Lord says to me: Go and stand at the gates of your people, through which the kings of Judah enter and leave, and at all the gates of Jerusalem.
And if you truly listen to me, says the Lord, bringing no burden through the gates of this city on the Sabbath day, and keeping the Sabbath day holy by doing no work on it.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Can I not do with you as this potter does, house of Israel? says the Lord. Behold, as clay is in the potter's hands, so you are in my hands, house of Israel.
Thus will I do to this place, says the Lord, and to its inhabitants, reducing this city to ruins.
And the next morning Pashhur brought Jeremiah out of the stocks, and Jeremiah said to him: The Lord has not called your name Pashhur, but Wandering Captive.
And you, Pashhur, and all who live in your house will go into captivity. You will go to Babylon, and there you will die and be buried, you and all your friends to whom you prophesied lies.

And I said, “I will not mention the Lord’s name or speak in his name anymore.” But in my heart it became like a burning fire blazing through my bones. I grew weary on every side, and I cannot keep quiet.
And I will strike all the inhabitants of that city, both people and animals, with a great plague, and they will die.
For if you truly carry out this command, kings who sit on David’s throne will enter through the gates of this house and ride in chariots and on horses, the king himself, his servants, and his people.
But if you do not carry out these commands, I swear by myself, says the Lord, that this house will become a ruin.
Woe to the one who builds his house without righteousness and his upper rooms without justice, who makes his neighbor work for him for nothing and does not pay him his wages.
If he had stood in my council, he would have made my people hear my words and turned them from their evil ways and their evil conduct.
Can a person hide in a hiding place without my seeing him? says the Lord. Do I not fill heaven and earth? says the Lord.
Are not my words like fire, says the Lord, and like a hammer that shatters rock?

And the Lord showed me two baskets of figs standing before the Lord’s temple, after Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon had taken captive Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, along with the officials of Judah, the craftsmen, the locksmiths, and the nobles from Jerusalem, and brought them to Babylon.
One basket contained very sweet figs, like early-ripening figs, and the second basket contained foul-tasting figs that could not be eaten because they were so bad.
And the Lord said to me, “What do you see, Jeremiah?” And I said, “Figs: sweet figs, very sweet, and bad figs, very bad, which cannot be eaten because they are so bad.”
And I will make the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the voice of the bride, the sound of the millstone and the light of the lamp disappear from among them.
And this whole land will become a ruin and a wasteland, and they will serve those nations and the king of Babylon for seventy years.
And all the kings of Zimri, and all the kings of Elam, and all the kings of Persia.
The sound of the shepherds’ lament and the cry of the rams of the flock, for the Lord has destroyed their pastures.
And I will make this house like Shiloh, and I will make this city a curse among all the nations of the earth.
And the priests and the false prophets said to the officials and to all the people, “This man deserves a sentence of death, because he prophesied against this city, as you heard with your own ears.”
And King Jehoiakim, all his warriors, and all his officials heard all his words, and they sought to kill him. When Uriah heard this, he was afraid and fled and went to the land of Egypt.
After another two full years, I will bring back to this place all the vessels of the Lord’s house that Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon took from this place and carried to Babylon.

And Jeconiah son of Jehoiakim, king of Judah, and all the captives of Judah who went to Babylon, I will bring back to this place, says the Lord—Jeconiah and the captives of Judah—for I will break the yoke of the king of Babylon.
Go, speak to Hananiah and say, “Thus says the Lord: You have broken wooden yokes, and I will make iron yokes in their place.”
And Jeremiah the prophet said to Hananiah the prophet, “Now listen, Hananiah: the Lord did not send you, and you have vainly led this people to put their hope in falsehoods.”

“And I will appear to you,” says the Lord, “and restore you from captivity. I will gather you from all the nations and from all the places where I scattered you,” says the Lord, “and bring you back to the place from which I took you captive.”
“Singers and the sound of merrymakers will come forth from them. I will multiply them, and they will not decrease; I will spread them out, and they will not dwindle.”
“For I have given every thirsty soul drink and filled every hungry soul.”
“In those days they will no longer say, ‘The fathers ate sour grapes, and the children’s teeth were set on edge.’”
Where King Zedekiah confined him, saying, “Why do you prophesy and say, ‘Thus says the Lord: Look, I am giving this city into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will capture it’?”
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
“This city has provoked my anger and wrath from the day they built it until today, so that I would wipe it away from my sight.”

Thus says the Lord: “In this place, of which you say, ‘It is desolate, without people or animals,’ in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem, in the desolate places where there are no people, no inhabitants, and no animals, there will again be heard

Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: “Go to Zedekiah king of Judah and say to him, ‘Thus says the Lord: This city will certainly be handed over to the king of Babylon, and he will capture it and burn it with fire.’”

“But you will die in peace. Just as they mourned your fathers, the former kings who came before you, so they will mourn you, saying, ‘Alas, alas, lord!’ And they will lament you, for I have spoken great things,” says the Lord.
The word of the Lord came to me and said:
Therefore thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: “The descendants of Jonadab son of Rechab will never lack a man to stand before me all the days of the earth.”
And Baruch said to them, “Jeremiah himself recited all these words to me, and I wrote them in the scroll with ink.”
And the king ordered Jerahmeel the king’s son, Seraiah son of Azriel, and Shelemiah son of Abdiel to seize Baruch the chief scribe and Jeremiah the prophet, but they went into hiding.

And Jeremiah took another scroll and gave it to Baruch son of Neriah, the chief scribe. He wrote in it, at Jeremiah’s dictation, all the words of the scroll that Jehoiakim king of Judah had burned in the fire, and still more words were added to it, beyond those.

And Jeremiah passed through the crowd and came and went, and they did not put him in prison. And Pharaoh’s army came out of the land of the Egyptians. When the Chaldeans who were besieging Jerusalem heard the news about them, they withdrew from Jerusalem.
Jeremiah came into the dungeon, into [?], and Jeremiah remained there for many days.

King Zedekiah sent for him and summoned him, and the king questioned him secretly in his house, saying to him, “Is there any message from the Lord?” And Jeremiah said, “Yes, there is.” And he said, “You will be handed over to the king of Babylon.”
And Shephatiah son of Mattan, Gedaliah son of Pashhur, Jehoahaz son of Shelemiah, and Pashhur son of Malchiah heard the words that Jeremiah spoke to all the people, saying:
And King Zedekiah said to Jeremiah, “There are some matters between me and the Jews who have fled to the Chaldeans. They might hand me over to them, and they might abuse me.”
And he blinded Zedekiah’s eyes and bound him with bronze chains to take him to Babylon.
And the Chaldeans burned the king’s house and the houses of the people with fire, and tore down the wall of Jerusalem.
The captain of the guard took him and said to him, “The Lord your God declared these calamities against this place.”

And all the Jews who were in the land of Moab, among the Ammonites, in Edom, and in all the other lands heard that the king of Babylon had left a remnant in Judea and had appointed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, as their overseer.

And in the seventh month, Ishmael son of Nethaniah, son of Elishama, of the royal family, and the king’s servants, and ten men with him came to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at Mizpah.
Away from the Chaldeans, for they were struck with fear of them, because Ishmael had killed Gedaliah son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had appointed over the land.

And he will set fire to the houses of their gods and burn them and carry them away captive. He will search the land of Egypt as a shepherd searches his clothing, and he will depart from there in peace.
The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning all the Jews who lived in the land of Egypt, who dwelt in Migdol, Tahpanhes, Memphis, and the land of Pathros, saying:

Did not the Lord remember the incense that you burned in the cities of Judah and outside Jerusalem—you, your fathers, your kings, your rulers, and the people of the land—and did it not come into his heart?
The word that Jeremiah the prophet spoke to Baruch son of Neriah when he wrote these words in a book from Jeremiah’s dictation, in the fourth year of Jehoiakim son of Josiah, king of Judah.
Proclaim the news in Egypt, sound it out in Migdol, give instructions in Memphis, and announce in Tahpanhes: Stand up and prepare yourself, for the sword has devoured your branches.
For there is news from Horonaim: destruction and great devastation.
Flee and save your lives, and become like a wild donkey in the wilderness.
Because you trusted in your strongholds, troubles will come, and you too will be captured. Chemosh will go into captivity, together with his priests and his rulers.
Moab has been put to shame, for it has been shattered. Cry out and shout, and proclaim at the Arnon that Moab has perished.
We have heard of Moab’s pride, for he has become exceedingly proud—his loftiness, his pride, and his arrogance—and his heart has become exalted.
Therefore raise a cry over Moab; proclaim the news throughout all the regions of Moab, over the men who have been torn, plucked, and blackened, and he will moan.
And Moab will perish from among the multitude, because he spoke boastfully against the Lord.
His place was deceived. Settle deeply, inhabitants of Dedan, for I have brought hardships [?] upon him, at the time when I punish him.
For grape gatherers have come against you, and they will leave you no remnant. Like thieves in the night, they will lay their hands on them.
Because of the Lord’s anger, it will not be inhabited, but will become entirely desolate. Everyone who passes through Babylon will be distressed and hiss at all its wounds.
And the Lord brought judgment upon her. Come, let us recount in Zion the works of the Lord our God.
And I will scatter his cavalry in you, and I will scatter his chariots and their riders upon you.
To make the land of Babylon desolate, so that no one will dwell in it.
For thus says the Lord of hosts, the God of Israel: The house of Babylon will stand like a threshing floor [?]; in a little while its harvest will come.
Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon devoured me, came against me, and tore me apart. He made me like an empty vessel; he swallowed me like a dragon and filled his belly with my delicacies.
How you have been defeated, Sheshach, and caught in a trap, you who were the boast of all the earth! How Babylon has become a desolation among all the nations!

And he will make her commanders and her wise men, her rulers and her army chiefs and her warriors drunk, and they will sleep an everlasting sleep and never wake, says the King, whose name is the Lord Almighty.
And Jeremiah wrote in one book all the calamities that were to come upon Babylon—all these words written against Babylon.

And in the ninth year of his reign, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon came to Jerusalem with his entire army and besieged it. He built walls around it, wall beside wall, out of squared stones.
And they captured the king and brought him to the king of Babylon at Riblah in the land of Hamath, and he passed judgment on him.
And there were two pillars, one Sea, and twelve bulls that stood beneath the Sea, which King Solomon had made in the house of the Lord. The bronze and all the bronze furnishings were beyond measure.
